A Brier score is the mean squared difference between the predicted probability and the observed binary outcome. Lower is better. Score only burns with resolved outcomes on the same indices and report coverage. Hypothetical yes/yes/yes/no gives 0.0161 for the model and 0.0100 for the guide's illustrative comparator. There are no observed FM² scores. [1]

7. FM², prediction with four dependent trials. The March 2026 design supersedes a 2024 configuration involving two different fuels. On viewer p. 10 it specifies Synergy Pro Navy; the older shortlist table on viewer p. 14 calls one candidate Natural Synergy Pro. Confirm grade, finish and lot before joining a comparison. With a nominally common limiting oxygen concentration for the four specimens, outcomes are dependent and the effective sample size is small. A Brier score can compare predictions on resolved indices. It cannot establish calibration from one four-burn mission. NASA gives qualitative expectations and a 24–26% expected LOC. The guide's 26%/1.5 percentage-point distribution is a teaching assumption. A shared oxygen threshold assumes that sufficient starting oxygen will produce sustained spread after a functioning igniter. Registering a separate ignition model would be necessary to estimate a distinct ignition-failure probability. A nominal attempt with no ignition and an invalid igniter have different scoring dispositions. A changed design or missing footage can also make an observation unscorable. The April FY 2027 budget request plans FM² lunar work for 2027. These documents provide the design and planning basis; an official result with traceable per-burn outcomes is still needed for scoring. Preserve each fraction exactly at the authors’ level of reporting: there is no basis here for a per-material denominator extrapolated from the total number of runs. response.answer:
Ferkul et al. specify four separate 2 × 20 cm exposed Synergy Pro Navy fabric strips at 8.2 ± 0.3 psia, with initial oxygen of 37%, 33%, 29% and 25%. Their concept gives an expected lunar limiting oxygen concentration of 24–26%. They expect the first three tests to burn to threshold and the fourth not to ignite. [1]

7. FM², prediction with four dependent trials. The March 2026 design supersedes a 2024 configuration involving two different fuels. On viewer p. 10 it specifies Synergy Pro Navy; the older shortlist table on viewer p. 14 calls one candidate Natural Synergy Pro. Confirm grade, finish and lot before joining a comparison. With a nominally common limiting oxygen concentration for the four specimens, outcomes are dependent and the effective sample size is small. A Brier score can compare predictions on resolved indices. It cannot establish calibration from one four-burn mission. NASA gives qualitative expectations and a 24–26% expected LOC. The guide's 26%/1.5 percentage-point distribution is a teaching assumption. A shared oxygen threshold assumes that sufficient starting oxygen will produce sustained spread after a functioning igniter. Registering a separate ignition model would be necessary to estimate a distinct ignition-failure probability. A nominal attempt with no ignition and an invalid igniter have different scoring dispositions. A changed design or missing footage can also make an observation unscorable. The April FY 2027 budget request plans FM² lunar work for 2027. These documents provide the design and planning basis; an official result with traceable per-burn outcomes is still needed for scoring.
